_meta.readme: The word-knowledge base behind the Vocabulary panel. Per word: the Persian gloss and band it is taught at (glossary.json), its IPA and syllable/stress count (senses.json, counted by tools/build_vocab_use.py), the collocations already in collocations.json, and the curated use layer - family, patterns, register, mistakes, Persian Bridge, wild passages and production prompts - from tools/vocab_use_src.py. No meaning, pronunciation or example is invented here: everything not authored is copied from a file that already shipped.

colls.ex: We can't afford a bigger flat.

pats.ex: I can't afford that car.
pats.fa: توان خرید آن ماشین را ندارم.

pats.ex: We can't afford to wait.

bad.bad: I can't afford buying a new laptop.
bad.good: I can't afford to buy a new laptop.
bad.why: Afford takes to + verb, not -ing: the second verb is a to-infinitive.

bridge.bad: It is not in my money.
bridge.why: Persian «به پول من نمی‌خورد» has no word-for-word English; afford is the verb that carries the whole idea.

use.task: Talk about something you would buy if you could.
use.frame: I'd love to … but I can't afford …
use.example: I'd love to travel in summer, but I can't afford the tickets.

allow / permit / enable.fa: اجازه دادن / مجاز داشتن / ممکن کردن

begin / commence / initiate.fa: شروع کردن / آغاز کردن / آغازگری کردن

colls.ex: Their last release set a benchmark for the industry.

pats.ex: We benchmark our prices against the market.
pats.fa: قیمت‌هایمان را با بازار مقایسه می‌کنیم.

bad.bad: We benchmark with our competitors.
bad.good: We benchmark against our competitors.
bad.why: Benchmark takes against: the comparison is a measurement against a fixed line.

use.task: Name one thing you measure to see if you are improving.
use.example: I benchmark my reading speed against last month's score.

bite off more than you can chew.w: bite off more than you can chew

bite the bullet.fa: با ترس و لرز تصمیم گرفتن

glosses.fa: با ترس و لرز تصمیم گرفتن

colls.ex: I borrowed a pen from Sara.

pats.ex: He borrowed the car from his neighbour.
pats.fa: ماشین را از همسایه‌اش قرض گرفت.

bad.bad: Can I borrow your pen to me?
bad.good: Can I borrow your pen?
bad.why: Borrow already means the thing comes to you, so adding to me doubles the direction; the sentence needs from only when the owner is named.

bridge.bad: Can you borrow me your pen?
bridge.good: Can you lend me your pen?
bridge.why: Persian «قرض دادن» and «قرض گرفتن» share a root, but English does not: lend is to give for a time, borrow is to take for a time.

use.task: Ask a colleague for something you will return.
use.example: Could I borrow your charger until the end of the meeting?

pats.ex: He broke his phone.

pats.p: break down / break up / break into
pats.ex: The car broke down on the motorway.

bad.bad: I broke my leg in the last year.
bad.good: I broke my leg last year.
bad.why: last year needs no in; in the last year means the past twelve months and needs a perfect tense.

use.task: Say what you do on a short break at work.
use.example: On my break I usually walk around the block.

pats.ex: We budgeted for two new laptops.
pats.fa: برای دو لپ‌تاپ نو بودجه گذاشتیم.

pats.ex: The project has a budget of ten thousand euros.

bad.bad: We must stay in the budget.
bad.good: We must stay within budget.
bad.why: Budget in this pattern takes no article: on budget, over budget, within budget.

use.task: Plan a small purchase for your home with a limit.
use.frame: I have a budget of … for …
use.example: I have a budget of two hundred for a new desk.

call it a day.fa: این کار را تمام‌شده اعلام کردن

colls.ex: That is very strong coffee.
They complained about the noise.

pats.ex: She complained about the delay.
He complained to the receptionist.

bad.bad: I complained the manager about the room.
bad.good: I complained to the manager about the room.
bad.why: The person takes to, the problem takes about; complain never takes a direct object.

bridge.why: Persian «از ... شکایت کردم» uses the same preposition as from, but English complains about a thing and to a person.

use.task: Complain politely about a problem in a hotel room.
use.frame: I'm afraid I have to complain about …
use.example: I'm afraid I have to complain about the air conditioning.

colls.ex: The building is in compliance with fire safety rules.

pats.ex: All staff must comply with the policy.
pats.fa: همهٔ کارکنان باید با سیاست پیروی کنند.

bad.bad: We must comply to the new rules.
bad.good: We must comply with the new rules.
bad.why: Comply takes with; compliance likewise is in compliance with a rule.

use.task: Say which rule at work or school you always follow.
use.frame: We are required to comply with …
use.example: We are required to comply with the data protection policy.

colls.ex: I feel confident about the interview.

pats.ex: She is confident about her decision.
I am confident that it will work.

bad.bad: I am confident on my answer.
bad.good: I am confident about my answer.
bad.why: The adjective takes about (or of) for the thing you are sure of; on belongs to depend on and rely on, not to confident.

bridge.why: Confident is an adjective, not a noun: the noun is confidence. Persian «اعتماد به نفس دارم» maps to I am confident, not I have confident.

use.task: Describe a decision you feel good about.
use.example: I am confident about my choice because I checked the prices.

cost an arm and a leg.w: cost an arm and a leg

pats.ex: I am curious about the result.
She was curious to see the message.

bad.bad: I am curious to the history of this city.
bad.good: I am curious about the history of this city.
bad.why: Curious about a subject, curious to do something.

use.task: Ask someone a question you really want answered.
use.example: I'm curious about how you learned to cook.

colls.ex: We met the deadline by two days.

pats.ex: The deadline for applications is Friday.
She works well to a deadline.

bad.bad: I finished the report in the deadline.
bad.good: I finished the report before the deadline.
bad.why: A deadline is a point in time: you finish before it or by it, never in it.

use.task: Describe the next thing you have to finish and when.
use.example: My deadline for the budget draft is Wednesday afternoon.

colls.fa: کاری را به کسی واگذار کردن
colls.ex: She delegated the report to a junior colleague.

pats.ex: He delegated the calls to his assistant.
pats.fa: تماس‌ها را به دستیارش واگذار کرد.

bad.bad: I delegated to him the task of calling clients.
bad.good: I delegated the task of calling clients to him.
bad.why: The thing comes after the verb and the person at the end with to; putting the person first sounds like Persian word order.

use.task: Name one job you could hand to someone else this week.
use.example: I could delegate the scheduling to the new intern.

finish / complete / conclude.fa: تمام کردن / کامل کردن / به نتیجه رسیدن

forbid / prohibit / ban.fa: ممنوع کردن / منع کردن / ممنوع کردن

colls.ex: The forecast says rain by evening.

pats.ex: Analysts forecast slower growth.
They forecast that prices will fall.

bad.bad: The weather forecast says it will rains.
bad.good: The weather forecast says it will rain.
bad.why: After will the verb has no -s: will rain.

use.task: Make a forecast about your week.
use.example: I forecast that Thursday will be the busiest day.

colls.ex: He gave a presentation to forty people.
Give an example of the past perfect.

give the benefit of the doubt.w: give the benefit of the doubt

colls.ex: She is good at explaining grammar.

hit the nail on the head.w: hit the nail on the head

pats.ex: Be honest with me.
He was honest about the mistake.

bad.bad: She is honest to me.
bad.good: She is honest with me.
bad.why: Honest with a person, honest about a thing.

bridge.why: Persian «به من گفت» takes an object, so say and tell get swapped: tell takes the person, say does not.

use.task: Tell someone an honest opinion about a film.
use.example: To be honest, the ending felt too long.

colls.ex: We implemented the plan in March.

pats.ex: The team implemented the change quietly.
pats.fa: تیم تغییر را بی‌سروصدا اجرا کرد.

bad.bad: We implemented the new system from last month.
bad.good: We implemented the new system last month.
bad.why: A finished action with a past time takes no from; from marks a starting point, not a when.

use.task: Describe a change you would make where you work.
use.example: I would implement a shorter Friday meeting because nobody reads the notes.

increase / rise / grow.fa: افزایش دادن / بالا رفتن / رشد کردن

colls.ex: Use a sharp knife for tomatoes.
She lent me her umbrella.

colls.fa: چیزی را به کسی قرض دادن

pats.ex: Can you lend me a hand?
He lent his bike to a friend.
pats.fa: دوچرخه‌اش را به دوستی قرض داد.

bad.bad: He lended me the book.
bad.good: He lent me the book.
bad.why: The past of lend is lent, not lended; lend / lent / lent.

use.task: Offer something of yours to somebody who needs it.
use.example: I can lend you my notes until Friday.

let the cat out of the bag.w: let the cat out of the bag

colls.ex: She leveraged her experience into a better role.

pats.ex: We leveraged the data to win the account.
pats.fa: از داده‌ها برای گرفتن حساب استفاده کردیم.

bad.bad: We leveraged on our contacts.
bad.good: We leveraged our contacts.
bad.why: Leverage is a verb that takes a direct object here; on belongs to rely on and depend on.

use.task: Name a skill you want to turn into an advantage.
use.frame: I want to leverage my … to …
use.example: I want to leverage my Persian to work with Iranian clients.

colls.ex: I listen to the news in English.

look / glance / stare.fa: نگاه کردن / نگاه گذرا / خیره شدن

colls.ex: He lost weight without trying.

pats.ex: The film made me cry.
The table is made of wood.

bad.bad: I did a mistake in the test.
bad.good: I made a mistake in the test.
bad.why: English makes a mistake; do belongs to homework, the dishes and your best.

bridge.bad: I want to do a decision.
bridge.good: I want to make a decision.
bridge.why: Persian uses one verb for both «تصمیم گرفتن» and «انجام دادن», and learners carry do into the fixed phrase. English decides with make.

use.task: Describe a choice you made recently.
use.frame: I made the decision to … because …
use.example: I made the decision to study in the morning because I'm too tired at night.

need / require / demand.fa: نیاز داشتن / لازم داشتن / تقاضا کردن

colls.ex: A loud noise woke the whole street.

pats.ex: Please be patient with the new staff.
Try to be patient about the delay.

bad.bad: I have not patient.
bad.good: I am not patient.
bad.why: Patient is an adjective; the noun is patience, and the negative of the noun is not patience.

use.task: Describe a time you had to wait for something.
use.frame: It was hard to be patient when …
use.example: It was hard to be patient when the bus was late again.

pats.ex: She is polite to everyone.
It is polite to say thank you.

bad.bad: He is polite with me.
bad.good: He is polite to me.
bad.why: Polite takes to for the person it is shown to.

use.task: Write a polite request to a neighbour.
use.example: Could you possibly keep the music down after ten?

pats.ex: He is always punctual for meetings.
pats.fa: او همیشه سر وقت در جلسه‌ها حاضر است.

bad.bad: I am punctual in the class.
bad.good: I am punctual for the class.
bad.why: Punctual for an event, punctual at work; in is the usual translation trap from «در کلاس».

use.task: Say why being on time matters where you work or study.
use.example: Being punctual matters because the whole team waits for you.

pats.ex: It was raining when we left.
The rain water filled the bucket.
pats.fa: آب باران سطل را پر کرد.

bad.bad: It rains heavily yesterday.
bad.good: It rained heavily yesterday.
bad.why: With a past time the verb is past: rained, not rains.

bridge.why: Persian «باران شدید» maps strong onto rain, but English weighs rain: it is heavy or light. Strong belongs to wind, coffee and arguments.

use.task: Describe the weather on a day you remember.
use.example: It was raining when we arrived, so we waited inside.

colls.ex: I highly recommend this restaurant.

colls.fa: چیزی را به کسی توصیه کردن

pats.ex: Can you recommend a good hotel?
I recommend booking early.
She recommends that we wait.

bad.bad: Can you recommend me a good restaurant?
bad.good: Can you recommend a good restaurant to me?
bad.why: Recommend is not like give: the thing comes first and the person takes to, or use recommend somebody something only for people (I recommend him for the job).

bridge.good: I recommend this book to you.
bridge.why: Persian puts the person first («به تو این کتاب را توصیه می‌کنم»); English recommends the thing and gives the person to.

use.task: Recommend a place in your city to a visitor.
use.example: I'd recommend the old bazaar because it is quieter in the morning.

reduce / diminish / decrease.fa: کاهش دادن / کم کردن / کاهش یافتن

pats.ex: You can rely on her to be early.

bad.bad: You can rely her.
bad.good: You can rely on her.
bad.why: The verb rely needs on; the adjective reliable does not.

use.task: Describe someone you can depend on.
use.example: I can rely on my brother because he always keeps his word.

colls.ex: You can rely on the offline dictionary.
I'd like to make a reservation for two.

pats.p: make a reservation for + number / time
pats.ex: She made a reservation for eight o'clock.
We reserved a table by the window.

bad.bad: I want to take a reservation.
bad.good: I'd like to make a reservation.
bad.why: A reservation is made, not taken; take is for a seat, a break or a photo.

use.task: Book a table for four at eight o'clock.
use.frame: I'd like to make a reservation for …
use.example: I'd like to make a reservation for four at eight, please.

rub someone up the wrong way.w: rub someone up the wrong way

pats.p: run + object (a company, a meeting, a check)
pats.ex: She runs a small studio.
pats.fa: او یک استودیوی کوچک را اداره می‌کند.

pats.ex: We ran out of milk.

bad.bad: He runs a marathon yesterday.
bad.good: He ran a marathon yesterday.
bad.why: The past of run is ran, not runs; with yesterday the sentence needs the past form.

use.task: Describe something you have run out of this week.
use.example: I ran out of coffee on Tuesday morning.

colls.ex: He did not say a word all evening.

show / reveal / disclose.fa: نشان دادن / آشکار کردن / افشا کردن

colls.ex: He fell into a deep sleep.

spend / invest / squander.fa: خرج کردن / سرمایه‌گذاری کردن / هدر دادن

colls.ex: Involve the stakeholders before the design is fixed.

pats.ex: She is a stakeholder in the project.
pats.fa: او در این پروژه ذی‌نفع است.

bad.bad: The stakeholders of the project agreed.
bad.good: The stakeholders in the project agreed.
bad.why: A stakeholder is a person with a stake in something: in, not of.

use.task: Say who would care about a change you want to make.
use.example: The main stakeholders in the new timetable are the parents and the teachers.

stand the test of time.fa: از آزمون زمان سربلند بیرون آمدن

pats.p: take + noun (a break, a photo, a seat)
pats.ex: Let's take a break.
It takes twenty minutes to get there.
pats.fa: بیست دقیقه طول می‌کشد تا برسیم.

bad.bad: I take a shower every morning.
bad.good: I take a shower in the morning.
bad.why: Take a shower is correct English; the mistake this pair catches is time: every morning (habit) versus in the morning (part of the day).

use.task: Say how long your journey to work or school takes.
use.example: It takes forty minutes to get to the office by bus.

take it with a pinch of salt.w: take it with a pinch of salt

take the law into your own hands.w: take the law into your own hands

take with a pinch of salt.w: take with a pinch of salt

colls.ex: The engine runs at a high temperature.

the ball is in your court.w: the ball is in your court

colls.ex: High staff turnover usually means low pay.

pats.ex: The firm has a turnover of two million.
pats.fa: شرکت گردش مالی دو میلیونی دارد.

bad.bad: The company has a turnover of two millions.
bad.good: The company has a turnover of two million.
bad.why: Million, thousand and hundred stay singular after a number: two million, not two millions.

use.task: Explain why people leave jobs, in one sentence.
use.frame: High turnover is often caused by …
use.example: High turnover is often caused by long hours and no training.

colls.ex: Wait for me at the corner.
A strong wind blew the door shut.
Do not be worried about mistakes.

bridge.why: «اشتباه کردم» uses the verb for doing, but English mistakes are made. The same verb pair covers a decision, a plan, a promise and an effort.
Discuss takes its object directly; about belongs to talk about and argue about. This is the most common -about of all.

bridge.bad: She is married with a doctor.
bridge.good: She is married to a doctor.
bridge.why: «ازدواج کرد با» translates with, but English marries to a person. Married with children is a different, correct phrase.
Depend, rely and concentrate all take on; of belongs to consist of and be afraid of.
Arrive at a place, arrive in a city or country - never to, which belongs to go to and get to.

bridge.good: He explained the problem to me.
bridge.why: Explain, describe and suggest do not take a person as their first object; the person comes after to.

bridge.bad: Can you suggest me a book?
bridge.good: Can you suggest a book to me?
bridge.why: Suggest takes the thing, then to the person. Recommend works the same way.
Interested in, good at, afraid of, proud of: the adjective chooses the preposition, and Persian «علاقه‌مند به» does not decide it.
Prefer A to B. Than appears only with the comparative: I like tea more than coffee.

bridge.bad: I have a rest every afternoon.
bridge.good: I take a break every afternoon.
bridge.why: «استراحت کردن» is take a break or have a rest, but have a rest is British and rarer; take a break is the natural phrase in most contexts.
Delicious is already absolute, like perfect and freezing: it does not take very. Absolutely delicious is the emphatic form.
Learn by heart exists but is dated in most varieties; memorize or learn off by heart are clearer. Keeping the phrase is not wrong, it just dates the sentence.
Tell takes the person; say takes the words. Say me is never English, whatever the Persian sentence looks like.

bridge.bad: She informed me about the delay.
bridge.good: She informed me of the delay.
bridge.why: Inform takes of, or a that-clause. About belongs to tell and warn.
Agree is a verb, not an adjective: no am. «موافقم» looks like a state, but English says I agree.
Age is be, not have: Persian «۲۵ سال دارم» uses having, English uses being.
Home takes no to after a verb of movement: go home, come home, get home.
Since with a point in the past needs the present perfect; the continuous sounds like a temporary stay.

bridge.bad: I will call you when I will arrive.
bridge.good: I will call you when I arrive.
bridge.why: After when, if, before and after, the future is the present tense: when I arrive.
Everybody, everyone and each take a singular verb in English, even though they mean a group.

wild.text: Sara presented her ideas confidently during the meeting. She felt confident about the numbers, and the team trusted her because she was honest about what she did not know.
wild.question: What does 'confidently' tell us about Sara?
options: She spoke in a self-assured way.
She spoke in a quiet voice.
wild.why: Confidently describes how sure she sounded, not how fast or how loudly she spoke.

wild.text: Guest: I made a reservation for two nights under the name Ahmadi. Receptionist: I can see it here. Guest: I'm afraid I have to complain about the room - the window does not close.
wild.question: What does the guest do after checking the reservation?
options: Make a complaint about the room.
wild.why: To complain about something is to make a complaint; the guest reports the window, not a bill.

wild.text: The forecast promises heavy rain across the north by evening, with strong wind on the coast. Drivers are asked to leave more time for their journey.
wild.question: What kind of rain does the forecast describe?
wild.why: English weighs rain: heavy or light. The passage says heavy, and strong belongs to the wind in the next clause.

wild.text: Hi all, a quick update before the deadline. We implemented the new booking form on Monday and the first numbers look good. Please keep the budget in mind if you order anything else this week. Thanks, Reza
wild.question: What happened on Monday?
options: The new booking form was put into use.
wild.why: To implement something is to put it into use; the form was not planned again, it went live.

blurb.en: The words of an ordinary day: home, people, places, time, numbers and the small verbs that hold a sentence together.
blurb.fa: واژه‌های یک روز معمولی: خانه، آدم‌ها، جاها، زمان، عدد و فعل‌های کوچکی که جمله را سر پا نگه می‌دارند.

blurb.en: Airports, rooms, roads and the weather that changes the plan.
blurb.fa: فرودگاه، اتاق، جاده و هوایی که برنامه را عوض می‌کند.

blurb.en: The body, the doctor, sleep, sport, feelings and the relationships that keep a person well.
blurb.fa: بدن، دکتر، خواب، ورزش، احساس‌ها و رابطه‌هایی که آدم را سالم نگه می‌دارند.

blurb.en: Clothes, sizes, the shop and the language of how something looks and fits.
blurb.fa: لباس، سایز، مغازه و زبانِ این‌که چیزی چه‌طور دیده می‌شود و چه‌طور می‌نشیند.

blurb.en: Shopping for food, cooking it, ordering it and staying somewhere it is served.
blurb.fa: خرید غذا، پختنش، سفارش دادنش و اقامت جایی که سرو می‌شود.

blurb.en: Phones, apps, online life and the words of the things that keep getting faster.
blurb.fa: گوشی، برنامه، زندگی آنلاین و واژه‌های چیزهایی که مدام تندتر می‌شوند.

blurb.en: Meetings, money, contracts and the language of a working day, from the office to the bank.
blurb.fa: جلسه، پول، قرارداد و زبان یک روز کاری، از دفتر تا بانک.

blurb.en: School, university, essays and the register an assignment expects.
blurb.fa: مدرسه، دانشگاه، مقاله و لحنی که یک تکلیف انتظار دارد.

blurb.en: Music, the news, the way people describe each other, and the idioms that make a sentence sound lived-in.
blurb.fa: موسیقی، خبر، این‌که آدم‌ها همدیگر را چه‌طور توصیف می‌کنند و اصطلاح‌هایی که جمله را طبیعی می‌کنند.

blurb.en: Buying, returning, paying, and dealing with the offices and services around a purchase.
blurb.fa: خریدن، پس دادن، پرداختن و سر و کله زدن با اداره‌ها و خدماتِ یک خرید.

scenario.en: A connection that did not wait

lines.en: I missed my connecting flight because the first one was late. My luggage is still tagged to Shiraz.
I can see the delay on your ticket. There is another departure at six; I can move your reservation to it at no charge.
That saves the trip. Do I need a new boarding pass?
You do, and it will print at the gate. Your suitcase stays checked through, so you only carry the carry-on.
Is there time for sightseeing near the terminal?
Two hours is enough for the old quarter, but keep your passport with you and be back before boarding.

question.prompt: Why did the passenger miss the connecting flight?
question.why: The connection was missed because the first flight was delayed.

travel.note: The scenario is a missed connection: the vocabulary is travel, flight and reservation, not office English.

scenario.en: The bag that went to the wrong city
scenario.fa: چمدانی که به شهر اشتباه رفت

lines.en: My checked baggage did not arrive. I waited at baggage claim until the belt stopped.
What was your connecting flight, and was the layover short?
Fifty minutes. The gate was at the far end of the terminal.
That is usually enough. I can see the suitcase was sent to the wrong city - it arrives on the nine o'clock flight.
Can it be delivered to my hotel, or must I come back for it?
We deliver it tonight. Keep this reference, and put the essentials in your carry-on baggage next time.

question.prompt: Where did the suitcase go?
question.why: Baggage service says it was sent to the wrong city and arrives tonight.

scenario.en: The room above the kitchen

lines.en: I booked a double room for three nights, but the noise from the kitchen keeps waking me up.
I am sorry about that. The air conditioning unit is above that room and it runs all night.
Could I move to a quieter room? I do not mind the stairs.
There is a twin room on the top floor, with a pillow and a spare blanket already there. Breakfast is included.
That works. What time is check-out on Sunday?
Eleven, but you can leave your luggage at reception after that.

question.prompt: Why is the guest's room noisy?
options: The air conditioning unit above it
question.why: The unit above the room runs all night, which is what wakes the guest.

scenario.en: The bus that does not take the bridge

lines.en: Does this bus go to the harbour, or do I need the metro?
It goes there, but not today - the bridge is closed for repairs.
So what is the quickest way? I have a ferry at four.
Take the tram to the last stop, then a taxi for the final kilometre. A bicycle would be faster than the bus right now.
And the ticket - do I pay on the tram?
There is a machine at the stop. Keep the ticket; inspectors check.

question.prompt: Why can't the bus take the bridge today?
question.why: The bridge is closed, so the tram and a taxi are the quickest way.

scenario.en: Smoke in the stairwell

lines.en: The smoke alarm went off and there is smoke in the stairwell. Should we evacuate?
Leave by the emergency exit on the left, not the lift. Is anyone injured or unable to walk?
My neighbour has a burn on her hand from the kitchen; she needs first aid.
The ambulance is outside. Take the bandage from the kit by the door and keep her warm.
The fire extinguisher cabinet is locked.
I have the key. Stay outside and do not go back in for anything.

question.prompt: How should the resident leave the building?
question.why: The fire officer says to use the emergency exit, never the lift.

scenario.en: The forecast changes the walk
scenario.fa: پیش‌بینی هوا برنامهٔ پیاده‌روی را عوض می‌کند

lines.en: Is the ridge walk still on? The forecast mentioned a storm.
It did, and there is fog on the summit already. We move the walk to the valley, where it is mild and dry.
Will it rain? I only brought a light jacket.
Drizzle until noon, then sunny. The wind is the real problem today, not the temperature.
And tomorrow? I would rather see the autumn colours in clear weather.
Tomorrow is cold but clear - good light, no humidity, and no thunder.

question.prompt: Why is the ridge walk moved to the valley?
options: There is fog and wind on the summit
question.why: Fog on the summit and strong wind are why the walk changes.

scenario.en: Finding the entrance on the wrong side
scenario.fa: پیدا کردن ورودی از سمت اشتباه

lines.en: I am looking for the main entrance, but every door on this side is locked.
You are on the back of the building. Go straight to the corner, turn left at the roundabout, and the entrance is opposite the signpost.
Is it far? I am parked behind the bank.
Two minutes. The lift inside is next to the stairs; the office is on the third floor.
And the exit for the car park?
Same door, then across the road - the one beside the kiosk.

question.prompt: Where is the main entrance?
options: Opposite the signpost, after the roundabout
question.why: Go straight, turn left at the roundabout; the entrance is opposite the signpost.

scenario.en: Joining a class that is already full
scenario.fa: ثبت‌نام در کلاسی که پر شده

lines.en: I want to join the evening swimming class, but the app says it is full.
It is, for now. Most people come for the gym and leave the pool at seven, so there is space then.
I also do running twice a week. Would cycling help my knees?
It would - low impact, and you can keep the running for the weekend. Do you play any ball sport?
Table tennis, badly. Is there a group here?
Thursday nights. Bring your own bat; we have the table and the balls.

question.prompt: Why can't the member join the evening swimming class?
question.why: The class is full until the gym crowd leaves at seven.

scenario.en: The sauce that caught on the pan

lines.en: That smells good. What is in the sauce?
Tomato, garlic and a little honey - I tasted it twice before it was sweet enough.
Did you roast the garlic first? It gets sweeter in the oven.
I fried it, and the pan was too hot, so it caught. I had to start again and stir the whole time.
Use a heavier pot next time and keep the heat low. Is the fish ready?
Two more minutes. Could you slice the lemon and put it on the plate?

question.prompt: What went wrong with the sauce?
options: The pan was too hot and it caught
question.why: The pan was too hot, so the garlic caught and the sauce had to start again.

scenario.en: A table, an allergy and a bill

lines.en: We booked a table for two at eight. Could we sit away from the door?
Of course. Before you order - is there an allergy in the party?
Yes, nuts. What would you recommend from the main course?
The grilled fish is mild and has no nuts. The starter of the day is spicy, so I would avoid it.
We will take the fish and a still water. Can we split the bill?
Yes, two receipts. The tip is not included, so it is up to you.

question.prompt: What must the kitchen avoid for this guest?
question.why: There is a nut allergy in the party, so the waiter recommends the fish.

scenario.en: The first week somewhere new

lines.en: Sorry - where is the kitchen, and when does everyone have lunch?
There, behind the stairs. We eat at one, because the afternoon meeting starts at two.
Who do I ask about a key, and why is this door always locked?
Ask Sam; she has a key for everyone. It is locked because the printer is inside.
Thanks. Something else - how do I get to the station from here?
You go left at the corner, and if you see the park you have gone too far.

question.prompt: Where is the kitchen?
question.why: The colleague points behind the stairs, and lunch is at one.

scenario.en: Two mornings that do not match
scenario.fa: دو صبحی که به هم نمی‌خورند

lines.en: I wake up at six and get up straight away, so I can have breakfast before the traffic.
I set an alarm for seven and still do not get up. I skip breakfast and take a shower instead.
Who makes breakfast in your house?
Nobody. I buy something on the way. In the evening I cook, and my brother does the dishes.
Do you go to bed early?
Never. I read a book until midnight, so I am tired all week.

question.prompt: What does Ben skip in the morning?
question.why: Ben sets an alarm, does not get up, and skips breakfast.

scenario.en: A flat with one problem after another
scenario.fa: آپارتمانی با یک مشکل پس از دیگری

lines.en: The window in the bedroom does not close, and the radiator under it stays cold.
The window needs a new handle. I will bring one and check the balcony door too.
Also, the lamp in the living room flickers, and the wardrobe door came off its rail.
Send me a photo of the wardrobe. Is the fridge working, at least?
The fridge is fine. The shower is not - the water stays cold for a long time.
Then it is the boiler. I will book someone for Thursday; keep the key with you.

question.prompt: What is wrong with the shower?
question.why: The water stays cold, so the landlord suspects the boiler.

scenario.en: Cleaning before the guests arrive

lines.en: You tidy up the living room and I will mop the floor, but please do not forget to dust the shelf.
I already loaded the dishwasher, but there is a spill under the sink that needs a cloth.
Use the one in the drawer. After that, fold the laundry and put it in the wardrobe.
Should I preheat the oven now, or wait until they arrive?
Now. The chicken takes an hour, and I still have to chop the vegetables.
Fine. I will take out the trash before they ring the bell.

question.prompt: What will Ali do before the guests arrive?
question.why: Ali takes out the trash before the bell rings.

scenario.en: Introducing everybody at a wedding

lines.en: That is my mother next to the door, and my father is the one with the camera.
And the little boy who keeps running between the tables?
My nephew. His sister, my niece, is the one in blue - she is a twin, actually.
So your brother is the tall man talking to my wife?
Yes, and the woman beside him is my sister-in-law. My grandmother is the one everyone is queuing to greet.
Your family is much bigger than mine. I have one cousin and no siblings at all.

question.prompt: Who is the little boy running between the tables?
question.why: The boy is her nephew; his twin sister is the girl in blue.

scenario.en: Where to find everything in a new town
scenario.fa: چیزها را در شهر تازه کجا پیدا کنیم

lines.en: Is there a pharmacy near the market? My son has a fever.
There is one on the corner, next to the bakery. The supermarket is opposite the bank.
And a park? He needs some air.
The garden behind the mosque is quieter, and there is a cafe by the gate.
What about a hospital, just in case?
The hospital is on the main street, past the post office - ten minutes by taxi from the village road.

question.prompt: Where is the pharmacy?
options: On the corner next to the bakery
question.why: The pharmacy is on the corner, next to the bakery.

scenario.en: The library card and the bus stop

lines.en: I want a library card. Which documents do I need?
A ticket with your address - a utility bill is enough - and your passport.
Is the museum on this street free on Fridays?
It is, and the square in front of it has a market at the weekend. The bus stop is by the traffic light.
How do I cross? There is no crosswalk near the corner.
Use the pedestrian bridge past the post office; the sidewalk on this side is closed for works.

question.prompt: What does the visitor need for a library card?
options: A ticket with the address and a passport
question.why: A utility bill with the address and a passport are enough.

scenario.en: A deadline, a weekend and a late train
scenario.fa: مهلت، آخر هفته و قطار دیرکرده

lines.en: The deadline is Friday at noon. Is that still possible?
Friday is tight, but I can send the draft tomorrow afternoon and the final version a day later.
Tomorrow is a holiday. What about the weekend?
I work Saturday morning, so the weekend is not lost. The last hour is always the quiet one.
Good. How many weeks until the second phase starts?
Two weeks from now, in the new month - I will send the calendar.

question.prompt: When is the deadline?
question.why: The deadline is Friday at noon, and the draft comes tomorrow afternoon.

scenario.en: Choosing between two flats

lines.en: The first flat is cheaper, but the rooms are small and the street is loud.
The second is more expensive, yet it is quiet, clean and close to the park.
Is the kitchen modern? I cook a lot, so a good stove is important.
It is new. The bathroom is old, but the water is hot and the heating is strong.
And the balcony - big or small?
Small but sunny. For a young couple it is the easier flat to love.

question.prompt: Which flat is quieter?
question.why: The second is more expensive but quiet, clean and close to the park.

scenario.en: A week of small decisions
scenario.fa: یک هفته پر از تصمیم‌های کوچک

lines.en: I want to learn to cook, but I never find the time.
Start with one dish. Buy the ingredients, read the recipe twice, and give yourself an hour.
And if it goes wrong? I hate wasting food.
Then write down what you did, and change one thing next time. Do you remember the soup you made?
I try to forget it. My brother still talks about it.
Ask him to help. Two people in a kitchen finish twice as fast.

question.prompt: What does Sahar suggest first?
question.why: One dish, the ingredients, the recipe twice, and an hour.

scenario.en: Splitting a bill three ways

lines.en: What is the total? We are three people and I want to split it.
One hundred and twenty thousand. That is forty each, exactly.
I only have a fifty. Can you give me ten back?
Of course. Two of you pay by card and the third in cash, if that is easier.
It is. And the first item on the receipt - was that the soup?
It was the second. The first was the salad, at half the price.

question.prompt: How much does each of the three people pay?
question.why: One hundred and twenty split three ways is forty each.

scenario.en: Painting a room in daylight
scenario.fa: رنگ کردن اتاق در نور روز

lines.en: I want the living room light gray, not white - white looks cold here.
Then we keep the ceiling white and the wall light gray. Do you want the door dark blue or the same gray?
Dark blue would be too much with the brown sofa.
Agreed. A beige curtain and a green plant will warm it up without another colour on the wall.
What about the small room? It is always dark.
Then cream, or a pale yellow - both hold the light better than gray.

question.prompt: Which colour is the living room wall?
question.why: The wall is light gray; the ceiling stays white and the door is not dark blue.

scenario.en: Enough for eight people

lines.en: We are eight for dinner. Is one chicken enough?
Barely. I would cook two, and a dozen eggs for the salad.
How much rice? I never judge it right.
A handful per person, so roughly two cups. Add a few extra for the children.
And the cake? The recipe says a spoonful of cinnamon.
A spoonful is plenty. Double the recipe if you want leftovers for tomorrow.

question.prompt: How much rice does the helper suggest?
question.why: A handful per person is roughly two cups for eight people.

scenario.en: A call that keeps dropping

lines.en: My calls keep dropping. The signal shows two bars and then the line goes dead.
Is it everywhere, or only at home? Check whether the network is weak indoors.
At home, mostly. I also get no notification when a message arrives.
Open the settings and look at the account - the notification sound may be off, and voicemail is full.
If I send you an attachment, can you check the line from your side?
Send a screenshot to this inbox and I will call you back on a different number.

question.prompt: What else is wrong besides the dropped calls?
question.why: The notification sound may be off and the voicemail is full.

scenario.en: The week nobody enjoyed
scenario.fa: هفته‌ای که هیچ‌کس از آن لذت نبرد

lines.en: You look tired and a little sad. Is everything all right?
I am exhausted, and honestly a bit disappointed. The project was cancelled on Friday.
That is frustrating. Were you angry with the decision?
Not angry - more confused. I felt proud of the work, and then it was gone.
It is normal to feel hopeless for a day. Are you nervous about the next one?
A little. But I am grateful the team said so early.

question.prompt: Why is Kian disappointed?
question.why: The project was cancelled on Friday, after he had been proud of the work.

scenario.en: Where it hurts

lines.en: Where does it hurt - the chest, the back, or the shoulder?
My back, low down, and sometimes my left leg.
Does the pain reach the knee or the ankle?
To the knee. And my neck is stiff when I turn my head.
Any numbness in the fingers or the toes?
No, but my right shoulder aches when I lift my arm above my head.

question.prompt: Where does the patient feel the pain most?
question.why: The pain is low in the back and reaches the left knee.

scenario.en: A cold that will not go

lines.en: I have had a cough and a fever for five days, and the medicine I bought is finished.
Do you have a headache or a stomach ache as well?
A headache in the evening. No stomach ache.
This looks like flu, not a simple cold. Take the syrup at night and rest; if the fever stays, see a doctor.
Do I need a prescription for the pills?
Not for these, but the pharmacy cannot sell the stronger ones without one.

question.prompt: What does the pharmacist think it is?
question.why: Five days of fever and cough looks like flu, not a cold.

scenario.en: A check-up that finds something

lines.en: Your blood pressure is high again. Any headache, or swelling in the ankles?
Some swelling, and I tire quickly. The prescription ran out last week.
I will refill it at a lower dose and book a check-up in a month. Is the pharmacy still the one on the corner?
Yes. Is this chronic, or will it get better?
It is manageable, not curable - and the side effect you mentioned should fade with the lower dose.
Should I take the medicine with food?
With breakfast, and keep the insurance card with the referral.

question.prompt: What will the doctor do with the prescription?
options: Refill it at a lower dose
question.why: The doctor refills it at a lower dose and books a check-up.

scenario.en: Three nights of bad sleep

lines.en: I have insomnia again. I go to bed late, wake up at three and cannot get back to sleep.
What is the last thing you do before bedtime - screen time, or work?
Email, usually. I am exhausted by Friday and I nap at my desk.
Set an alarm for the same wake up time, and give yourself an hour to unwind with no screen.
Will exercise help? I have no energy for the gym.
A short walk is enough. Sleep, food and hydration do more for a mood than one hard workout.

question.prompt: What is the coach's first advice?
options: Keep one wake-up time and no screen before bed
question.why: The routine is the fix: one wake-up time and an hour to unwind.

scenario.en: The colleague who went quiet

lines.en: You seem withdrawn this week. Are you overwhelmed by the new deadline?
A bit anxious, and reluctant to say so. I am self-conscious about asking for help twice.
That is understandable. What would make the week feel manageable?
Fewer meetings, and someone to share the reporting. My motivation is fine; the volume is not.
I can move two meetings. How is your mood outside work?
Better. I have empathy for the team, but I need to protect my own focus too.

question.prompt: What does the colleague ask for?
question.why: The volume, not the motivation, is the problem.

scenario.en: Dressing for a cold wedding
scenario.fa: لباس پوشیدن برای عروسی در سرما

lines.en: I need something for a winter wedding. The dress I have is too light for the season.
A coat over it, or a heavier dress with long sleeves. Do you prefer a skirt or trousers?
Trousers, and comfortable shoes - the ceremony is outdoors.
Then boots, a scarf and gloves, and no sandals whatever the forecast says.
The jacket I own has a broken zipper and a missing button.
Bring it in; I can replace both before Thursday. Wear the belt you like and we will match the colour.

question.prompt: What does Sara need for the winter wedding?
question.why: The ceremony is outdoors, so boots, a scarf and gloves.

scenario.en: The jacket that is the wrong size

lines.en: I bought this jacket in medium, but it is tight across the shoulders. Do you have a large?
Let me check the shelf. If not, the fitting room has two similar ones on sale.
I would rather exchange it than take a refund. I like the quality.
An exchange is fine with the receipt. The price tag is still on, so there is no problem.
Is there a discount on the second one?
Twenty percent, but it is a different brand and it runs small.

question.prompt: Why does the customer want an exchange?
options: The jacket is too tight across the shoulders
question.why: The medium is tight, so a large or an exchange is needed.

scenario.en: What is left in the kitchen

lines.en: There is bread, cheese and one egg. Should we order pizza instead?
No need. I can make an omelette and a salad, and there is soup in the freezer.
Do we have rice? I could cook kebab if there is meat.
The meat is finished, but there is chicken. Buy some yogurt and a lemon on the way home.
And coffee - we are out of it.
Get tea too. We drink more tea than coffee in this house.

question.prompt: What can they cook without going shopping?
question.why: There is bread, cheese, one egg and soup in the freezer.

scenario.en: The stall at the end of the street

lines.en: Are the peaches ripe? Last week they were hard.
These are from yesterday, and the watermelon is sweet. Try a slice.
I will take a kilo of peaches and one pomegranate.
The pomegranates are small but full of juice. The figs are better value.
Then a box of figs as well, and two lemons for the tea.
The strawberries are finished, but the cherries arrive tomorrow.

question.prompt: What arrives at the stall tomorrow?
question.why: The strawberries are finished, but the cherries arrive tomorrow.

scenario.en: A stew with what the garden gives

lines.en: The tomatoes are ready, and there is more spinach than we can eat.
Perfect for a stew. I need onion, garlic and two carrots as well.
Take the eggplant too - it is small this year but sweet.
Should I add potato, or is it heavy enough?
A sweet potato would be lighter. There is chili if you want heat.
Just one, and some lettuce for the side. The peas are still frozen, so they can wait.

question.prompt: What is ready in the garden?
question.why: The tomatoes are ready and there is more spinach than they can eat.

scenario.en: A project that needs one more week
scenario.fa: پروژه‌ای که یک هفته بیشتر می‌خواهد

lines.en: The client wants the report on Monday. Can the team meet that deadline?
The research is done, but the budget section needs the finance figures. One extra week would make it solid.
Then I will ask for a week and offer a shorter summary on Monday.
That works. I will schedule a meeting with the client and update the task list today.
Who is leading the presentation?
The new colleague, with my support. It is good for his career, and he knows the product.

question.prompt: Why does the report need one more week?
options: The budget section needs the finance figures
question.why: The research is done; the budget figures are what is missing.

scenario.en: Minutes, a grievance and a promotion

lines.en: Before the meeting, I need the agenda circulated and the minutes from last week.
They are ready. I flagged two deliverables that will miss the milestone unless we delegate part of the workflow.
I will tackle that with the stakeholder and escalate the budget line if needed. Anything else?
One personal item: I submitted a grievance about the overtime on my payroll.
I saw it, and we will follow up this week. On a better note, your appraisal is positive - promotion is on the table.
That is good to hear. I will sign off the brief this afternoon.

question.prompt: What did the team member submit?
question.why: The grievance is about the overtime on the payroll.

scenario.en: Two people describing their work

lines.en: I am a pharmacist, so I spend the day explaining medicine to people.
My sister is a nurse and my father was a farmer. Different worlds.
What do you do? You said something about design.
I am a designer, but I trained as an architect. The pay is better in design.
Do you work with a programmer or an engineer?
Both, and a photographer. A small team, so everyone does two jobs.

question.prompt: What does Tom do now?
question.why: He trained as an architect but works as a designer.

scenario.en: A card that will not work abroad
scenario.fa: کارتی که در خارج کار نمی‌کند

lines.en: My card was refused in Turkey. The balance is fine, so I do not understand it.
The account is blocked for foreign payments. Did you travel without telling us?
I did. I need to withdraw cash and pay a hotel bill tomorrow.
I can lift the block now. Carry some cash as well, and keep the receipt for the exchange rate.
Is there a fee for the transfer?
A small one, shown on your statement. The discount applies only to payments in the local currency.

question.prompt: Why was the card refused?
question.why: The account is blocked for foreign payments and the clerk lifts the block.

scenario.en: The mortgage the bank would not agree to

lines.en: The bank refused the mortgage. They said my income is fine but my expenditure is too high.
Do you have other debt - a loan, or an installment plan on a car?
One loan, and a credit card balance I have been paying off slowly.
Clear the card first. It affects your credit score more than the loan does.
And the deposit? They asked for a bigger one because of inflation.
Twenty percent is the realistic figure. I will build a budget that shows your cash flow over six months.

question.prompt: Why did the bank refuse the mortgage?
options: There is no deposit at all
question.why: The income is fine; the expenditure, the loan and the card balance are the problem.

scenario.en: The exam the whole class worried about
scenario.fa: امتحانی که کل کلاس نگرانش بود

lines.en: I left my notebook at home, so I have no notes for the lesson.
You can share with the student next to you, and write on paper for today.
Will the exam cover the whole semester or only the last subject?
The last two terms. Bring a pencil, a ruler and your schoolbag with the book, nothing else.
And the project? Is the grade separate from the exam?
Yes. The library has the books you need, and the schedule is on the board.

question.prompt: What will the exam cover?
question.why: The exam covers the last two terms.

scenario.en: An essay, a deadline and a citation

lines.en: I want to extend the deadline for my essay by three days. The literature review took longer than I planned.
That is possible. Submit what you have on Friday and the full assignment a week later.
Do I need the abstract before the introduction?
No. Write the introduction, then the methodology, and revise the abstract last.
The citation format is confusing me. Which reference style does the department use?
The one in the syllabus. And please check the plagiarism rules before you paraphrase.

question.prompt: What does the student want?
options: Three more days for the essay
question.why: The essay needs three more days because the literature review took longer.

scenario.en: Reading a paper that contradicts itself
scenario.fa: خواندن مقاله‌ای که با خودش تناقض دارد

lines.en: The study claims to demonstrate a correlation, but the data do not indicate any significant change.
Does it establish causation, or merely rely on previous findings?
It relies on previous work and fails to distinguish the two variables. The conclusion is not coherent.
Then your critique should emphasize that, and justify why the method is inadequate.
I can illustrate it with their own table, and predict what a larger sample would show.
Do that, but keep the tone appropriate - the authors are prominent in the field.

question.prompt: What is wrong with the paper?
options: It claims a correlation the data do not show
question.why: The data indicate no significant change, so the claim does not hold.

scenario.en: A result nobody can replicate
scenario.fa: نتیجه‌ای که کسی نمی‌تواند تکرار کند

lines.en: Your hypothesis is clear, but the methodology does not let anyone replicate the experiment.
We acknowledge that. The anomaly came from one instrument, and we tried to substantiate it with a second sample.
That discrepancy needs to be delineated, not explained away. Can you quantify the error?
We can allocate two more weeks and incorporate the raw data in an appendix.
Good. Be careful not to conflate correlation with causation - your conclusion currently does.
I will articulate that more carefully in the revision.

question.prompt: What can the authors do about the anomaly?
options: Quantify the error and add the raw data
question.why: They can allocate two weeks and put the raw data in an appendix.

scenario.en: A letter that must sound like a letter
scenario.fa: نامه‌ای که باید لحن نامه داشته باشد

lines.en: Here is the draft. I wrote 'ask for' and 'get', which sounds too informal for a client.
Change them to 'request' and 'obtain', and use 'regarding' instead of 'about'.
Should I write 'prior to' or 'before' in the second paragraph?
Either is correct, but 'prior to' is more formal. Keep 'sufficient' for 'enough' and 'additional' for 'extra'.
And the closing - 'yours sincerely' or 'dear Sir or Madam'?
Use 'dear Sir or Madam' only if you do not know the name; otherwise 'yours sincerely'. Please submit it before noon.

question.prompt: Which word is more formal than 'ask for'?
question.why: The manager replaces 'ask for' with 'request' and 'get' with 'obtain'.

scenario.en: How sure can a report sound
scenario.fa: یک گزارش تا چه حد می‌تواند مطمئن باشد

lines.en: The draft says the policy will definitely work. Is that too strong?
It is. 'Arguably' or 'presumably' is fairer, and 'on the whole' softens the summary.
The data are mixed, so I could say the result is 'a mixed blessing'.
To some extent, yes. Admittedly the sample is small; that should appear before the conclusion.
Should I keep 'undoubtedly' anywhere?
Only for the figure itself. Everything else is 'largely' or 'comparatively' - and 'all things considered' closes it well.

question.prompt: Which word is too strong for the draft?
question.why: 'Definitely' is too strong; 'arguably' and 'presumably' are fairer.

scenario.en: A contract clause read aloud
scenario.fa: خواندن یک بند قرارداد با صدای بلند

lines.en: The clause states that the tenant is liable for repairs, albeit only for damage caused by negligence.
Notwithstanding that, the landlord must still maintain the roof - insofar as the statute applies.
Precisely. Furthermore, the deposit is refundable thereafter, whereby the balance is returned within thirty days.
And pending the inspection? Can they withhold the whole amount?
No. Save for documented costs, the remainder is due; barring a dispute, the matter ends there.
Then I will sign, subject to the aforementioned changes.

question.prompt: What must the landlord still do?
question.why: The tenant is liable for negligence, but the landlord maintains the roof.

scenario.en: Arrested, charged, and out on bail
scenario.fa: بازداشت، اتهام و آزادی با قید وثیقه

lines.en: My brother was arrested last night. They say he was involved in an offense near the station.
Has he been charged, and is he in custody or out on bail?
In custody. There is a witness, but no evidence that I know of.
Then we ask for bail tomorrow. The judge will look at the verdict history and whether he is liable to flee.
He has a residency permit and a job. Does that help?
It does. If the court imposes a fine, we can settle out of court on the civil claim.

question.prompt: What will the lawyer ask for tomorrow?
question.why: They ask for bail, since there is a witness but no evidence yet.

scenario.en: Renewing a licence before the deadline

lines.en: I need to renew my licence. Which form do I fill in at this counter?
This one, with your identification and a photocopy of the certificate.
Do I need an appointment, or can I submit it today?
Today is fine. There is a fee, and the signature must match the passport.
My address changed last month. Does that affect the application?
It does - bring proof of the new address, or the office will reject it and you will have to complain in writing.

question.prompt: What happens if the address proof is missing?
options: The office will reject the application
question.why: Without proof of the new address the office rejects it.

scenario.en: A result that will not replicate

lines.en: We ran the experiment three times and could not replicate the original correlation.
Was the control group the same size, and did the sample change between runs?
Same protocol, different sample. The statistics suggest the effect is small, not absent.
Then say so plainly. A robust finding survives peer review; a fragile one needs replication.
The method is accurate but slow. We are prototyping an algorithm to shorten it.
Keep the evidence separate from the tool. Causation is not the same as a faster pipeline.

question.prompt: What could the team not do?
question.why: Three runs could not replicate the original correlation.

scenario.en: A review of a very quiet film

lines.en: The film is subtle rather than vivid, and the dialogue is candid about a mundane marriage.
Is that compelling enough for a Saturday page? Readers want a reason to go.
The reason is the nuance. Nothing is lavish or profound; it is honest, and quietly resilient.
Your last review was skeptical about films like this.
I was, and I still am about the ending, which is obscure on purpose. But the acting is meticulous.
Keep that ambivalence - it is fairer than praise, and less tedious than a summary.

question.prompt: How does the critic describe the film?
question.why: It is subtle, candid about a mundane marriage, and meticulously acted.

scenario.en: The farm that lost a chicken
scenario.fa: مزرعه‌ای که یک مرغ گم کرد

lines.en: One chicken is missing, and the dog will not stop barking at the hedge.
A fox, most likely. Did you see tracks near the sheep?
No, but the goat is nervous and the horse was restless all night.
Put the ducks and the turkey inside, and keep the rabbit hutch shut.
The cat is useless. It slept through the whole thing.
Cats are like that. The geese are better guards than any dog.

question.prompt: What probably took the chicken?
question.why: A fox is most likely, and the geese guard better than the dog.

scenario.en: A portrait that is too realistic

lines.en: The exhibition opens in three weeks. Is the portrait finished?
Almost. The composition works, but the texture of the canvas is too smooth for the style.
The gallery wall is bright; a darker shade behind it would help the contrast.
I was thinking abstract shapes in the background, and a sketch of the hands in the corner.
That could be a masterpiece, or a distraction. What is the inspiration?
A painting I saw as a child. I want the design to feel drawn, not photographed.

question.prompt: What is wrong with the portrait?
options: The canvas texture is too smooth
question.why: The texture is too smooth for the style the artist wants.

scenario.en: A quarterly report nobody read

lines.en: The turnover is up, but the margin is down. What does the forecast say for next quarter?
Flat, unless we streamline procurement. The workload is already high, and overtime is on the payroll.
Then delegate the reporting and escalate the invoice problem to compliance.
I can prioritize two deliverables, but the milestone needs a stakeholder decision.
Set up a meeting, sign off the agenda, and take minutes. I want the quarterly report short enough to read.
One page. I will forecast the conservative number.

question.prompt: What is down while turnover is up?
question.why: Turnover is up but the margin is down, and the forecast is flat.

scenario.en: The meeting where nobody decided
scenario.fa: جلسه‌ای که در آن کسی تصمیم نگرفت

lines.en: We need to reach an agreement today and make a decision on the budget.
I want to raise an issue first: we cannot meet a deadline we never agreed to.
Fair. Let us draw a distinction between the report and the launch, and set a goal for each.
I will take responsibility for the report if someone else does the research.
I can carry out the research and keep track of the figures. We should also hold a meeting with the client.
Then I will place the order for the equipment, and pay the bill this week.

question.prompt: What must they do today?
question.why: They need to reach an agreement and make a decision on the budget.

scenario.en: The new neighbour everybody likes
scenario.fa: همسایهٔ جدیدی که همه دوستش دارند

lines.en: The new neighbour is friendly and remarkably patient with the children.
He is also punctual, which is rare in this building. Is he reliable?
Very. He is honest about what he can and cannot fix, and never careless with tools.
Some people find him a bit serious. I would say confident, not arrogant.
He is shy until you talk about football, then he is talkative and genuinely humorous.
A good neighbour. His wife is the ambitious one - she runs two shops.

question.prompt: How is the new neighbour described?
question.why: He is friendly, patient, punctual and reliable.

scenario.en: The phone that forgot its password
scenario.fa: گوشی‌ای که رمزش را فراموش کرد

lines.en: I cannot log in. The screen asks for a password I do not remember, and the battery is nearly dead.
Plug in the charger first. Then tap 'forgot password' and check your username.
Will that delete my backup? I have photos I never uploaded.
No, but sync them when you are back online. Turn on Wi-Fi before you download the update.
The app also asks for a permission it does not need. Should I allow it?
Check the privacy settings and refuse. A screenshot app wants your whole profile, which is suspicious.

question.prompt: What is the first step?
options: Charge the phone and reset the password
question.why: Charge it, tap 'forgot password', and check the username.

scenario.en: A town arguing about its river
scenario.fa: شهری که بر سر رودخانه‌اش بحث می‌کند

lines.en: The council approved the landfill beside the river. Is that sustainable?
No. Waste disposal there would contaminate the water and destroy the habitat of an endangered species.
They argue it reduces emissions from transport.
Marginally, while the carbon footprint of the site grows. Renewable energy and conservation would do more.
What about the drought last summer? Does it change the plan?
It should. Flooding and drought in one year is exactly what climate change looks like here.

question.prompt: Why is the landfill a bad idea?
options: It would contaminate the water and harm a habitat
It is too far from town
question.why: Waste disposal there would contaminate the river and destroy an endangered habitat.

scenario.en: A deal that was a blessing in disguise

lines.en: Losing that contract was a blessing in disguise - we were at the mercy of one client.
A far cry from where we started. Still, the terms left much to be desired.
By no means a disaster. We took it with a grain of salt and kept abreast of the market.
Now we are at the helm, and the new team will stand the test of time if we do not sit on our hands.
Agreed. Let us set the record straight with the bank and meet halfway on the repayment.
Then I will take a back seat on hiring and focus on the product.

question.prompt: How does the investor see losing the contract?
question.why: Losing it ended their dependence on one client.

scenario.en: The pitch that broke the ice

lines.en: I will break the ice with a question: how many of you have missed a deadline this month?
All of us. So far so good, then - but the software looked complicated.
It is a piece of cake once you set it up. The training is free, and support answers out of the blue, even on Sundays.
Our manager wants to see eye to eye with the IT team before signing.
Then the ball is in your court. I can join that meeting and hit the nail on the head about costs.
Let us call it a day. I will make up my mind by Thursday.

targets: hit the nail on the head
the ball is in your court

question.prompt: How does the presenter begin?
options: With a question to break the ice
question.why: The presenter breaks the ice with a question about missed deadlines.

scenario.en: A meeting that needed brass tacks
scenario.fa: جلسه‌ای که به اصل مطلب نیاز داشت

lines.en: Let us cut to the chase: the launch is up in the air and the board wants a date.
To make matters worse, two suppliers are on thin ice and the contract is a storm in a teacup for legal.
Then get down to brass tacks. Read between the lines of their email and tell me what they really want.
Money, by the book. They will not throw caution to the wind, and they will not go the extra mile for free.
Pull no punches with them. If they swallow their pride, we have a golden opportunity.
I will leave no stone unturned and report on Friday. No picnic, but doable.

question.prompt: What does the board want?
question.why: The launch is up in the air and the board wants a date.

scenario.en: A headline nobody can stand behind

lines.en: The headline says the minister was allegedly involved. Where is the evidence?
Two sources, one document, and a witness who will not go on the record.
Then it is an allegation, not a fact. Cite the document and fact-check the statistics before we publish.
The investigation is solid, but the leak came from inside the ministry.
That is the story. Write a feature story, keep the poll out of the lead, and let the editorial take the position.
Understood. The broadcast version will be shorter, and the podcast can carry the testimony.

question.prompt: What does the editor demand before publishing?
question.why: An allegation needs evidence, and the statistics must be fact-checked.

scenario.en: A song that needs one more verse
scenario.fa: ترانه‌ای که یک بند دیگر می‌خواهد

lines.en: The melody is good, but the chorus arrives too early and the lyrics repeat themselves.
Then we slow the tempo for one verse. The drum comes in after the second line.
I want the guitar quieter there so the voice carries. Is the piano in the same key?
It is. We can add a violin on the last note, and keep the harmony simple.
The band plays it better live than on the album - the rhythm is looser.
Then record the concert. A microphone in the hall beats a studio take with no audience.

question.prompt: What arrives too early in the song?
question.why: The chorus arrives too early and the lyrics repeat themselves.

scenario.en: A walk before the rain

lines.en: Is the path to the lake open? The map shows a river crossing.
It is, but the bridge is old. Follow the branch of the trail along the valley, under the cliff.
And the forest on the other side - is there a cave?
A small one, near the desert edge. Do not go in if it rains; the soil above it moves.
The sky looks heavy. How long until the storm?
An hour. Take the stone path back, and watch for lightning on the mountain.

question.prompt: Why should the hiker stay out of the cave in the rain?
question.why: The guide says the soil above the cave moves when it rains.

scenario.en: Choosing the exact word

lines.en: You translated 'angry' as 'irritated'. He was furious, not mildly annoyed.
I chose the softer word because the sentence says he spoke calmly. Should I use 'furious' and keep the contrast?
Yes. And here - 'he looked at her' became 'he stared at her'. That changes the meaning.
'Glance' would be closer. One quick look, no threat.
Exactly. The scene is ordinary, not strange - it should read typical, almost boring.
Then I will replace 'peculiar' with 'ordinary' and reduce the adjectives by half.

question.prompt: Which word fits 'he was very angry'?
question.why: 'Furious' is the strong word; 'irritated' is too soft for the scene.

scenario.en: The flat that needs sorting out
scenario.fa: آپارتمانی که باید سر و سامان بگیرد

lines.en: I am looking for a flat, and I have run out of time before the contract ends.
I can look into two agencies. Do you want me to come across on Saturday?
Please. I need to sort out the deposit first, and figure out how much the move costs.
Put off the furniture until you see the place. You can pick up a cheap table later.
The landlord turned down my offer, so I may have to give in on the price.
Do not give up yet. We will go over the contract and rule out the hidden fees.

question.prompt: What has the tenant run out of?
question.why: The contract is ending and there is no time left to look.

scenario.en: Two friends who drifted apart
scenario.fa: دو دوست که از هم دور شدند

lines.en: We used to keep in touch every week, and then we drifted apart. I miss the friendship.
There was a misunderstanding about the wedding, and neither of us apologised.
I was jealous, honestly. You had a partner and a new flat, and I felt left behind.
I should have been more supportive. Trust works both ways, and I assumed you did not care.
Can we make up? Not with a big gesture - just coffee on Fridays.
Deal. Commitment to a small thing is easier than a promise to change everything.

question.prompt: What caused the distance between them?
question.why: A misunderstanding about the wedding, and neither of them apologised.

scenario.en: The laptop that will not start

lines.en: My laptop will not start. The charger works, but the screen stays black.
Does the battery light come on? Try a different socket and hold the power button for ten seconds.
Nothing. I have the files backed up on a hard drive, luckily.
Then we test the memory first, and the router is not involved. Is the software under warranty?
The hardware is, for one more month. There is also a virus warning every time I open the browser.
Leave it with me. I will update the program, check the database of errors, and call you.

question.prompt: What is wrong with the laptop?
question.why: The screen stays black even with a working charger.

scenario.en: A shelf that will not stay level

lines.en: The shelf is not level and the bracket is loose. I think the wall is broken behind it.
Measure twice first. Hand me the tape measure and the drill.
Do we need a screwdriver or a wrench for the bracket?
A screwdriver, and longer screws. The plug in the wall is too small, so it pulls out.
There is a leak under the sink too. Can we fix that today?
We can tighten the pipe and tape it, but the proper repair needs a plumber. Assemble the shelf first.

question.prompt: Why does the bracket pull out of the wall?
options: The plug in the wall is too small
question.why: The plug is too small, so longer screws are needed.

scenario.en: A restructuring nobody expected
scenario.fa: بازساختاری که کسی انتظارش را نداشت

lines.en: The projection shows a deficit next quarter. Which initiative can we cut without hurting productivity?
None of them cheaply. The restructuring is already in the roadmap, and the merger needs due diligence.
Then look at overhead and procurement. Our market share is stable, but the churn worries shareholders.
We can outsource support and optimize the process, with clear accountability and a benchmark for each KPI.
Do it without burning the team. Retention is cheaper than hiring, and the outlook depends on it.
Agreed. I will iterate on the plan and bring the escalation path to the board on Monday.

question.prompt: What worries the shareholders?
question.why: Market share is stable, but the churn worries shareholders.
